angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 951,022 km at 120.34 pc = 0.11 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 8.3100 +/- 0.0139 mas (same row, RUWE 1.03): 120.34 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 1.367 +/- 0.061 solar radii from Kendall et al. 2026, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of NGTS-34 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2026MNRAS.547f2189K/abstract): 951,022 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 1.266 +/- 0.063 solar masses from Kendall et al. 2026, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of NGTS-34 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2026MNRAS.547f2189K/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 6134 +/- 55 K from Kendall et al. 2026, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of NGTS-34 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2026MNRAS.547f2189K/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Kendall et al. 2026, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of NGTS-34 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2026MNRAS.547f2189K/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/ngts-34.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.269, rounded to two decimals

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, coloured from the star's Gaia DR3 BP/RP spectrum (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
